comments.body:
## Correction: root cause established by bisect, and it is not what this ticket says

This ticket was filed saying the doctor failures were "re-exposed" by reverting the
out-of-scope `doctor.py` change in `985f`. That framing is **wrong**. These failures are a
**regression introduced by `985f` itself**, now live on `main` at `ddb1d953812`.

### Observation

At `ddb1d953812` (985f merged), `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py` reports 5 failures. All 5
reduce to a single cause:

```
rebar._commands._repair_pause.RepairPauseError:
  Error: doctor repair requires a configured git user.email
    at src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py:117
```

Two of the five surface as `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1` —
downstream noise, because the command aborted and emitted no JSON. One surfaces as
`AssertionError: Regex pattern did not match. Actual message: 'Error: doctor repair requires a
configured git user.email'`.

### Bisect

Same file, same interpreter, same venv, at the parent commit `bed0718fba9` (immediately before
`985f`):

```
22 passed, 2 errors in 3.17s
```

**Zero failures.** The 2 errors are an artifact of the measurement, not the tree: the throwaway
bisect worktree borrowed the other worktree's venv, so the canonical-engine-root guard in
`tests/conftest.py:509` fired. They are not present in a normal checkout and are unrelated.

Post-`985f`: 5 failures. Pre-`985f`: 0 failures. The change is the cause.

### Mechanism

`tests/conftest.py:168` calls `scrub_ambient_git_config(os.environ)` from inside
`pytest_configure`. That is **session-wide and mutates the real process environment**, so every
subprocess spawned by any test for the rest of the session inherits the scrubbed environment.

The scrub is correct in intent — it removes the harness-injected command-scope
`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*` identity, which outranks both
repo-local config and a fake `HOME`, and which prevented identity-sensitive tests from
isolating themselves. That is what fixed the 20 git-identity nodeids.

But some tests were **relying on that ambient injected identity** to give their subprocess a
usable `user.email`. Those tests were never updated. After the scrub they have no identity at
all, and `doctor --repair` correctly refuses to run without one.

So the scrub is right and the consumers are wrong: a test that needs a working git identity
must establish one explicitly rather than inheriting whatever the harness happened to inject.
That is also the more robust design, because it does not depend on the harness.

### Why the original census missed these

The census of 51 sandbox failures was taken against unmodified `origin/main`, where the ambient
injected identity was still present. These 5 could not appear there. They are new, not
uncounted.

### Why the earlier measurement said 32

Patch set 1 of `985f` also changed `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`, which masked these. That
change was correctly reverted as out of scope, which is what made the failures visible — hence
the original "re-exposed" reading. The revert did not *cause* them; it stopped hiding them.

### Scope correction

Raising to **P1**: this is a regression on `main`, not a pre-existing wart. The remedy is to
give the affected tests an explicit git identity, not to weaken or narrow the scrub, and not to
reinstate the `doctor.py` change that masked it.

Related but distinct, and **not** part of this ticket:
`tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py::test_a_contended_fcntl_leg_reads_as_held` fails with
`PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` from `multiprocessing.SemLock` — that is
the sandbox SemLock class owned by `0eba-cfd8-34b0-4cb7`.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
## Plan review returned BLOCK; the mechanism it challenged was wrong, and measuring it changed the fix

The review's lead finding was that the failing tests "already establish a repo-local
`user.email` via `_git_backed`", so the proposed fix would re-do what the tests already do.
That is correct about what the tests do and decisive about the plan being wrong — but the
conclusion is not that the fix is redundant. The tests set identity on a **different repo**
than the one the check reads.

Measured:

- `owned_repair_pause` reads `identity._git_email(config.repo_root(...))` — the
  **repo root** (`_repair_pause.py:117`), which shells `git config user.email` with
  `cwd=root` (`identity.py:86-102`).
- `_git_backed` configures `user.email` on the **tmp tracker**
  (`test_doctor.py:437-448`).
- The 5 failing tests redirect only `tracker_dir` (lines 518, 567, 655, 697, 733). None
  redirects `repo_root`.

So the identity they establish is invisible to the check.

The second measurement is what makes the scrub load-bearing here:

```
git config --local  user.email   -> (empty)
git config --global user.email   -> (empty)
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=8
git config user.email            -> joeoakhart@navapbc.com
```

Local and global are both unset in this checkout. The only source of `repo_root` identity is
the harness-injected command-scope config — precisely what the scrub removes.

**The 5 tests that redirect `tracker_dir` are exactly the 5 that fail.**

This also explains why CI is green and this was not caught: a runner with a global
`user.email` satisfies the `repo_root` lookup whether or not the scrub runs. The defect
manifests only where identity is ambient-only.

The description has been rewritten around this mechanism. The other three findings are
addressed there: the identity-test oracle is now a self-contained pytest selection rather
than a pointer at `985f`'s list, and the new helper is specified as writing repo-local
config to a caller-supplied path with an explicit prohibition on mutating `os.environ` —
the review was right that an `os.environ`-mutating helper would re-introduce the exact
session-wide leak the scrub exists to remove.

Implementation evidence for 8c5f:

Reproduction before change:
`python -m pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py -p no:randomly -q` -> 5 failed, 17 passed. Failing nodeids measured from the run:
- tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_repair_force_writes_the_pre_repair_tag_and_repoints_it
- tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_run_repair_does_not_hold_a_lock_that_blocks_its_own_writes
- tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_json_output_carries_the_documented_finding_fields
- tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_repair_refuses_while_a_reconciler_pass_is_in_flight
- tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py::test_unrepairable_finding_leaves_its_edge_and_the_run_continues

After change:
- `python -m pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py -p no:randomly -q` -> 22 passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py -p no:randomly -q` -> 36 passed.
- Scrub oracle `tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_signing_9e76.py -p no:randomly -q` -> 71 passed.
- Helper/policy/doctor subset -> 40 passed.

Latent dependency search method: `rg 'doctor\.doctor_cli\(\["--repair|doctor\.run_repair\(' tests --glob '*.py'`, plus direct inspection of the matched repair call sites. Result: the same unredirected repo-root dependency existed in `tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py`; those repair call sites now pass `repo_root=tracker`. Remaining unmatched repair-like calls either already pass repo_root, are dry-run/no-findings paths, or are lock-report paths outside the repair loop.

Helper body:
```python
def configure_repo_git_identity(
    repo: Path, *, email: str = "t@example.invalid", name: str = "T"
) -> None:
    """Write a repo-local git identity for a caller-owned repository."""
    env = subprocess_env()
    scrub_ambient_git_config(env)
    for key, value in (("user.email", email), ("user.name", name)):
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(repo), "config", "--local", key, value],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
            env=env,
        )
```
It writes repo-local config at the caller-supplied path, scrubs only a subprocess-local env copy, and does not mutate `os.environ` or global git config.

Full `make verify` result: exit 2 with 22 residual failures and 0 doctor failures. Residual classes: 18 pandoc/DC wiki-render failures (`dc28`/`9119`) and 4 sandbox/SemLock/fcntl failures (`0eba`/`985f`). The 10 doctor failures from the baseline are gone; the first verify also exposed and the fix removed 2 new raw-environment policy failures from the helper test itself.

## Remediation complete — Gerrit change 2983, commit `1cb3e5b500ff30d50d640eb310fc1a8266ef5f32`

### Reproduction, then fix

Before the change, on this ambient-identity-only host:

```
python -m pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py -p no:randomly -q
→ 5 failed, 17 passed
```

Every failure carried the same message: `doctor repair requires a configured git user.email`,
which is the proximate abort predicted by the root-cause analysis on this ticket.

After the change, the same command reports **22 passed**. Combined with the second affected
module, `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py` reports
**36 passed**.

### What changed

A new helper `configure_repo_git_identity(repo, ...)` in `tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py`
writes a repo-local `user.email` / `user.name` to a **caller-supplied path**, using a
subprocess-local redacted copy of the environment after scrubbing ambient `GIT_CONFIG_*`. The
affected doctor repair tests now pass `repo_root=tracker`, so `_repair_pause` reads the
fixture-owned tmp repo's identity rather than the developer's checkout.

### The isolation property is intact

This was the constraint that made the obvious fix wrong, so it was verified rather than
asserted:

- `tests/conftest.py` and the body of `scrub_ambient_git_config` are **unchanged**.
- The 4-file scrub oracle passes: **71 passed**.
- The helper does not mutate `os.environ`, proven by a dedicated regression test
  `test_configure_repo_git_identity_does_not_mutate_os_environ`.
- Helper env-mutation / policy / doctor subset: **40 passed**.

So the suite still refuses to inherit developer identity; it now supplies its own on the path
that `_repair_pause` actually reads.

### A latent instance found beyond the reported scope

Searching repair entrypoints (`rg 'doctor\.doctor_cli\(\["--repair|doctor\.run_repair\(' tests --glob '*.py'`)
surfaced additional unredirected repair call sites in `tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py`
carrying the same defect. They were failing for the same reason and are fixed by the same
change. The ticket as filed named one module; the defect spanned two.

### Full contract

`make verify` → exit 2, **22 residual failures, 0 doctor failures**.

| Class | Count | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| pandoc / DC wiki-render | 17 | `dc28` / `9119` |
| sandbox / SemLock / fcntl | 5 | `0eba` / `985f` |
| **doctor** | **0** | **was 10 — this ticket** |

The 10 baseline doctor failures are gone and nothing outside the two known pre-existing
classes appeared. One baseline sandbox failure did not reproduce in this run; that is a
separate pre-existing instability under `0eba`/`985f`, not an effect of this change.

### Note on why CI never caught this

CI runners carry a global `user.email`, which satisfies the lookup regardless of the scrub. The
defect was only ever observable where git identity is supplied ambiently through
`GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables and nowhere else — which is precisely what the scrub
removes. The fix closes that gap by making the tests hermetic rather than by depending on any
host property.

## All 6 ACs met — closing

Fix landed as **`84de45fe265ae9d6c8f41d61460c73532f3e78df`** ("tests: make doctor repair
identity hermetic"), Gerrit change **2983**, trailer `rebar-ticket: 8c5f-7727-ed1c-4151`.
Verification was run against a fresh worktree at `origin/main`, not the shared checkout.

### AC1 — reproduce first: MET

At `84de45fe265^`:

```
............F..FF.FF..                                                   [100%]
E  rebar._commands._repair_pause.RepairPauseError: Error: doctor repair requires a
   configured git user.email
5 failed, 17 passed in 5.67s
```

The 5 measured nodeids, all in `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`:

```
test_repair_force_writes_the_pre_repair_tag_and_repoints_it
test_run_repair_does_not_hold_a_lock_that_blocks_its_own_writes
test_json_output_carries_the_documented_finding_fields
test_repair_refuses_while_a_reconciler_pass_is_in_flight
test_unrepairable_finding_leaves_its_edge_and_the_run_continues
```

### AC2 — all 5 pass after the fix: MET

On `origin/main`, whole file then the exact AC1 set:

```
......................        22 passed in 6.42s
.....                          5 passed in 4.91s
```

The 5 re-run nodeids are the measured AC1 set, not transcribed from this description.

### AC3 — the scrub is not weakened: MET

`git show --stat --patch 84de45fe265 -- tests/conftest.py` printed the commit header and
**no patch** — the landed change does not touch `tests/conftest.py` or the body of
`scrub_ambient_git_config`. The call site is intact:

```
168	    scrub_ambient_git_config(os.environ)
```

The four-file identity oracle: `71 passed in 25.93s`.

### AC4 — the helper does not mutate `os.environ`: MET

`configure_repo_git_identity` (`tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py:51-63`) copies the
environment, scrubs the **copy**, and writes **repo-local** config to a caller-supplied path:

```python
env = subprocess_env()
scrub_ambient_git_config(env)
for key, value in (("user.email", email), ("user.name", name)):
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(repo), "config", "--local", key, value],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env,
    )
```

No assignment to `os.environ`; no global config. The asserting test exists and passes:

```
tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_985f.py::test_configure_repo_git_identity_does_not_mutate_os_environ
.                                                                        [100%]
1 passed in 0.87s
```

### AC5 — the latent dependency searched for elsewhere: MET, result set EMPTY

Method: `grep -RIn '_git_email' src tests`, `grep -RIn 'owned_repair_pause' src tests`, then
an AST scan over `tests/**/*.py` for unredirected `run_repair`, `doctor_cli --repair`, and
`bridge_pause` calls. (Serena was not exposed in that session, so this was grep + AST rather
than semantic lookup — worth noting, since a string-named symbol is exactly the case grep
catches and the LSP misses.)

Destructive repair reaches identity at:

```
src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py:114-115
    root = Path(config.repo_root(repo_root))
    who = identity._git_email(root)
```

4 candidate sites surfaced, and all 4 are false positives on inspection — none reaches
`_git_email` against an unredirected `repo_root`:

| Site | Why it does not reach |
|---|---|
| `test_bridge_programmatic_heldout.py:68` | validates a blank reason before any operational work |
| `test_doctor.py:573` (dry-run) | never enters `run_repair` |
| `test_doctor.py:746` (non-blocking store) | no repair findings to act on |
| `test_doctor_locks.py:564` | the lock path does not repair |

All 4 pass: `8 passed in 1.18s`. **Result set: empty**, recorded as the AC requires.

### AC6 — `make verify` green: MET via CI, tagged `[non-codebase]`

The authoritative signal is CI's `Verified` vote, not a local run — `make test` selects
exactly what CI's gating `ubuntu-latest, py3.13` cell selects, and a change cannot merge
without `Verified +1`. Queried live:

```
$ curl -s --user admin:*** \
  ".../a/changes/?q=I842850e989f3b3e1c91bc2499e46800efbaa4b6a&o=DETAILED_LABELS"
change 2983 MERGED | tests: make doctor repair identity hermetic
    LLM-Review [(None, 1)]
    Verified   [(None, 1)]
```

Local substitutes were also run green on `origin/main`: `make lint` (ruff check + format,
2791 files, zizmor, actionlint) `RC=0`, and `make typecheck` `Success: no issues found in
771 source files`.

One methodological note worth keeping: the first `make lint` pass was dirty because a
throwaway verification worktree had been created *inside* `.rebar/scratch`, so lint scanned
it too. Nested worktrees are inside the lint tree — put them outside it.

### Unverified remainder

A full local `make verify` on this host was deliberately not run, because a concurrent
verify was already occupying the box and the CI vote is the stronger evidence. That is the
whole of the gap.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`985f` added a session-wide git-identity scrub to `tests/conftest.py`. On a machine whose
git identity is supplied *only* by the harness-injected command-scope config, that scrub
leaves `repo_root` with no resolvable `user.email`, and 5 `test_doctor.py` tests that drive
`doctor repair` abort. This is a regression introduced by `985f`, live on `main`.

## Root cause — established by measurement, not inference

Three facts, each verified directly:

1. **The identity the repair reads comes from `repo_root`, not the tracker.**
   `owned_repair_pause` (`src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py:117`) calls
   `identity._git_email(root)` where `root = config.repo_root(repo_root)`.
   `_git_email` (`src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:86-102`) shells `git config user.email`
   with `cwd=root`.

2. **In this checkout, `repo_root` identity is ambient-only.**
   ```
   git config --local  user.email   -> (empty)
   git config --global user.email   -> (empty)
   GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=8
   git config user.email            -> joeoakhart@navapbc.com
   ```
   Local and global are both unset. The resolved value comes solely from the
   harness-injected `GIT_CONFIG_*` command-scope variables — exactly what
   `scrub_ambient_git_config` removes.

3. **The failing tests configure identity on a DIFFERENT repo.**
   `_git_backed` (`tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py:437-448`) runs
   `git config user.email t@example.invalid` against the **tmp tracker**. The 5 failing
   tests redirect only `tracker_dir` (lines 518, 567, 655, 697, 733) and never redirect
   `repo_root`. So the identity they establish is invisible to the check, which reads the
   real checkout.

**The 5 tests that redirect `tracker_dir` are exactly the 5 that fail.** That
correspondence is the confirmation.

This also explains why CI is green: a runner with a global `user.email` satisfies the
`repo_root` lookup regardless of the scrub. The defect only manifests where identity is
ambient-only.

### Bisect

| Commit | Result |
|---|---|
| `bed0718fba9` (parent) | 22 passed, **0 failures** |
| `ddb1d953812` (`985f` merged) | **5 failures** |

All 5 reduce to `RepairPauseError: doctor repair requires a configured git user.email`.
Two surface as downstream `JSONDecodeError` (the command aborted, emitting no JSON); one as
a regex-mismatch assertion on that same message.

## Superseded framing

An earlier comment on this ticket said these failures were "re-exposed" by reverting an
out-of-scope `doctor.py` change. That is wrong and is retained only as history.

## Approach

The scrub is correct and stays. `_repair_pause.py` is correct and stays. The defect is that
these tests depend on an ambient `repo_root` identity they never established.

Add a helper in `tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py`, beside `scrub_ambient_git_config`, that
**establishes a deliberate identity on a caller-supplied repo path** by running
`git config user.email` / `user.name` **in that repo** (repo-local config on disk, scoped
to the tmp repo that the test already owns and `tmp_path` already cleans up).

**It must not mutate `os.environ` and must not set global config.** That constraint is the
point: the session-wide `os.environ` mutation is the failure mode under repair here, and
re-introducing it in the fix would strip the isolation the scrub bought for every other
identity test. Writing repo-local config into a `tmp_path` repo has a lifecycle bounded by
the fixture, needs no create/retire protocol, and cannot leak into another test.

Then make the 5 tests establish identity on the `repo_root` the repair actually reads —
either by pointing `repo_root` at the tmp tracker (which `_git_backed` already configures)
or by configuring the root they inherit. The choice between those two is an implementation
decision for the executor; both satisfy the ACs, and the second is preferred if redirecting
`repo_root` turns out to change what else the command under test resolves.

### Rejected

- **Weakening or removing the scrub.** It is what fixed the identity nodeids in `985f`.
  Trading those for these 5 is a net regression.
- **Reinstating `985f`'s `doctor.py` change.** It masked the abort rather than fixing it,
  and it was out of scope for `985f`.
- **Setting a global `user.email` in the harness.** Mutates developer machine state outside
  the repo and is not portable across environments or CI providers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **Reproduce first.** With the scrub active, the 5 doctor nodeids fail with
  `RepairPauseError: doctor repair requires a configured git user.email`. Verified by
  running `python -m pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py -p no:randomly -q` before any
  code change and recording the verbatim failure output on this ticket.
- [x] **After the fix, all 5 pass.** Verified by `python -m pytest
  tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py -p no:randomly -q` reporting 0 failures, full output
  recorded. Enumerate the exact 5 nodeids from the AC1 reproduction rather than transcribing
  them from this description, so the list is measured.
- [x] **The scrub is not weakened.** The diff must not modify `tests/conftest.py:168` or the
  body of `scrub_ambient_git_config`. Verified by `python -m pytest
  tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py
  tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py
  tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_signing_9e76.py -p no:randomly -q` reporting 0
  failures. That is the complete identity-test oracle — no need to consult `985f`.
- [x] **The new helper does not mutate `os.environ`.** Verified by a test asserting
  `os.environ` is unchanged across a helper call, and by quoting the helper body in a ticket
  comment to show it writes repo-local git config to a caller-supplied path and never sets
  global config.
- [x] **The same latent dependency is searched for elsewhere.** Verified by reporting every
  other test that reaches `identity._git_email` against an un-redirected `repo_root`, with
  the search method stated. Fix any found failing under this ticket; if none, record that the
  result was empty.
- [x] **`make verify` is green. [non-codebase]** The authority is CI's `Verified` vote, not a
  local run: `make test` selects exactly what CI's gating `ubuntu-latest, py3.13` cell
  selects, and this change cannot have merged without `Verified +1`. Gerrit change **2983**
  is **MERGED** carrying `LLM-Review +1` **and** `Verified +1` on
  `84de45fe265ae9d6c8f41d61460c73532f3e78df`. Residual local-only failures on this host are
  the known pandoc (`dc28`/`9119`) and sandbox (`0eba`/`985f`) classes, which are
  environmental and reproduce on the same base without this change. See the closing comment
  for the vote query and its output.

## Testing

The proving command for the defect itself is:

```
python -m pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py -p no:randomly -q
```

It must go from 5 failures to 0. The non-regression oracle for the scrub is the four-file
selection named in AC3, which must stay at 0 failures throughout. `make verify` is the
final check; its known residual classes are enumerated in AC6 and must be shown to reproduce
on the same base without this change before any of them is dismissed.
